title: The Humble Intercessor

full_text:
A severe drought afflicted the city of Cairo for two years. The Nile failed to rise, the fields cracked into dust, and the famine was so dire that the grand scholars, viziers, and merchants gathered in the open desert outside the gates to hold public prayers for rain. Day after day, hundreds of dignitaries prayed in embroidered robes, but the sky remained like scorching brass, without a single cloud.

Among the crowd was an eminent sage named Malik. Watching the solemn gathering, his eye fell upon a humble, ragged laborer named Mubarak, an enslaved porter who stood quietly behind a sand dune, away from all public notice.

Mubarak fell prostrate upon the hot sand, his tears wetting the dust, and prayed with childlike simplicity: 'O Creator of all creatures! Look upon the little children who hunger and the weary beasts that thirst. By Your boundless compassion, send down the sweet rain upon the earth!'

Before Mubarak could rise to his feet, a cool wind stirred the desert sands. A small grey cloud appeared from the north, grew with miraculous speed, and within an hour, the heavens opened with a glorious, torrential downpour of rain!

The citizens rejoiced, shouting with joy as the water filled the dry canals.

Malik, having observed Mubarak’s prayer, followed the humble porter to the house of his master, a wealthy merchant. Malik purchased Mubarak’s freedom with a hundred gold dinars, intending to honor him as a holy sage.

When Mubarak learned that his secret devotion had been discovered, he wept in humble distress: 'O master, why have you brought me fame? The servant who loves his Creator desires only to serve in quiet humility, without the praise of men.' He departed into the countryside to tend the orchards of the poor, leaving Cairo to marvel at how a single pure heart in rags had saved an entire empire.
moral: True spiritual greatness dwells not in proud ranks or fine robes, but in the pure and humble heart.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Pious Black Slave"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
